[{"path":"README.md","content":"# TalkSprout

Reusable prompts for learning English with AI: choose a conversation coach, practice speaking, and turn completed chats into study material.

[Open TalkSprout](https://octopusgarage.github.io/talksprout/)

## Use the app

- **Start practice:** choose a collection and coaching style. Copy the full prompt into a new AI conversation, or read its short spoken opening aloud. A dismissible first-practice guide helps new users choose a coach.
- **Wrap-up & Review:** send a review prompt at the end of that same conversation to create notes, sentence practice, vocabulary, or self-test cards.
- **Quick access:** save a coach, scenario, format and interview pace as one combination, or share a link to that setup. The home page shows three saved combinations with an option to expand. Recently copied prompts appear in their own area; supplementary prompts have independent favorites. Private scenario background is never saved or included in links. Safe selections update the current URL without adding history entries. Local favorites, combinations and recent copies synchronize across windows.
- **Learning guides:** browse two separate shelves: ten companion guides organized into preparation, practice and review, and seven further readings: four complete methodology articles and three AI usage articles covering live voice, dedicated chats or bots, and global instructions. Five bot configurations and two global instruction blocks have individual copy buttons with manual fallback. Each shelf has bilingual search and topic filters. Articles focus on practical explanations and examples without source footers or external-link collections; companion guides include relevant prompt shortcuts. Cached articles work offline.
- **App sharing:** share TalkSprout from the header or Settings. Supported devices open the system share sheet; other browsers copy the app home link. A manual copy dialog is available if sharing or clipboard access fails. Shared app links exclude the current route and query parameters.
- **Settings:** choose the interface language, find installation help, share the app, and read the instructions.
- **Listening, reading & writing:** open the secondary entry below the speaking collections for 18 supplementary prompts, with six choices per direction. Tasks include dictation comparison, meeting notes, shadowing preparation, complex sentences, emails and notices, technical documentation, email replies, workplace messages, and summary/paraphrase practice. Each entry includes a decorative emoji and concrete use examples; three direction buttons keep the directory compact. Copy a prompt to your AI and supply material there. These prompts stay separate from coach search and review.

The interface supports Chinese and English. Prompt instructions are in English; review and learning-helper explanation defaults follow the selected interface language. Conversation coaches focus on English practice; request Chinese help from your AI when needed. English learning examples remain in English. TalkSprout provides prompts for your preferred AI app; it does not run an AI chat itself.

Supplementary links use `#learning` and `#learning?prompt=writing-feedback`. Details show preparation, usage and a single English prompt, without spoken openings or scenario settings. If the external AI cannot access a source, the prompt requests usable excerpts or transcripts. This app does not process links or files; audio/video compatibility depends on the chosen AI and has not been tested here.

## Conversation coaches

| Collection             | Modes                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Conversation coaches   | Natural Conversation Coach; Gentle Conversation Coach; Focused Correction Coach; Score and Rewrite Coach |
| Interactive coaching   | Role-play Coach; Debate Coach; Vocabulary Game Coach                                                     |
| Practice with material | Visual Description Coach; Retelling Coach                                                                |

Each mode defines how the AI teaches, when it corrects, and how the conversation continues. Open a coach's details to select an optional scenario before copying; leaving it unset preserves the original prompt.

## Practice scenarios

The scenario picker contains 160 presets across Everyday Life & Interests (31), Travel & Getting Around (13), Everyday Services (12), Tech Workplace Communication (48), and Software Engineering Interviews (56). Scenarios default to No preset and remain collapsed behind a single settings row. Open the picker to search in Chinese or English, browse grouped lists, and tap a scenario to fill the prompt with a hypothetical situation, roles, goal, and opening. Selecting another preset replaces the previous setup. Workplace presets retain unit references to the supplied 48-unit communication handbook.

Travel includes existing trip planning, transport, hotel and dining topics plus missing baggage, cancelled flights, room problems and incorrect orders. Everyday Services covers returns, deliveries, bills, housing, appointments and local services. Everyday social practice includes invitations, favours, boundaries, apologies and misunderstandings. These are hypothetical communication exercises; service policies, charges and outcomes must be confirmed rather than invented.

Scene browsing categories and coach suitability are separate: moving existing travel topics preserves their debate and vocabulary-game support. New service and travel problem-solving scenes use conversation or role-play coaches.

Expand Scenario settings to add up to 2,000 characters of optional background to the full prompt. This background is held only in the current sheet session, is not saved locally, and is included when you copy the full prompt to your external AI. The short spoken opening keeps the topic, role where applicable, and coaching loop; provide detailed background during the conversation.

Role-play Coach offers coached practice or mock interview pacing for technical interviews. Mock pacing defers feedback until review or finish; technical discussion and language feedback remain distinct. Other conversation coaches retain their correction styles. Debate and vocabulary games support everyday topics with their own interaction loops. Image/retelling coaches and post-conversation reviews do not use these presets.

TalkSprout generates prompts; it does not run code, grade actual hiring performance, or execute AI conversations.

Every coach has a full prompt and a short spoken opening, with sentence-by-sentence reading and an estimated reading time. Short forms preserve the core coaching loop but do not establish equal behavior across AI services.

## Wrap-up & Review

| Review                             | Purpose                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Complete Study Notes (recommended) | Cover the main topics, genuine corrections, useful sentences, vocabulary, and recall tasks.          |
| Sentences and Corrections          | Keep original wording, distinguish errors from optional improvements, and collect reusable patterns. |
| Vocabulary and Pronunciation Notes | Record contextual meanings, collocations, examples, and American IPA for selected key words.         |
| Review Cards and Self-Test         | Start with one useful card; request multiple cards when needed, with a separate answer key.                   |

Use **Current AI chat** in the original conversation. For another conversation, choose **Another transcript**, copy the template, and replace its placeholder with a speaker-labeled transcript before sending it to your AI. Do not paste your transcript into TalkSprout.

Each review also has a short **Spoken wrap-up** for the current chat. Request written material where supported; voice-only replies fall back to a brief oral recap. AI can review only the context it can access. Uncertain IPA needs verification and cannot establish how you pronounced a word.

## Navigation and local data

Phones use bottom navigation; desktop uses a sidebar. Only the content area scrolls. Prompt sheets keep the copy action visible and support browser Back, Escape, and focus restoration. A pending copy finishes before another write can start; switching formats or leaving a sheet clears its copy feedback. Existing collection links remain valid; a prompt link looks like `#collection/companions?prompt=daily-check-in`.

On touchscreens, swipe left from the rightmost 32 pixels and release after at least 72 pixels to close a sheet or return from a collection to the library. Top-level views stay in place. Vertical, multi-touch, text-field, and text-selection gestures do not trigger this action. Browser tests cover the application gesture logic; actual iOS Home Screen gesture behavior requires device testing.

Search and saved filters remain separate for practice, each practice collection, and review. The practice-home search covers all coaches; collection searches stay within that collection. Filters and scroll positions last for the current session, while favorites, saved combinations, bounded recent-copy metadata, guide dismissal and language preferences are saved on this device.

No account, API key, or analytics is required. TalkSprout does not receive or store AI conversations. Clearing browser data removes local preferences and favorites.

## Install and use offline

Open **Settings → Install app** for device-specific instructions. After a complete online visit and successful caching, prompts can be browsed and copied offline. External AI still requires a connection. Available updates wait for **Update now**. The app shows immediate progress, reopens once activation is confirmed, and briefly acknowledges completion. If activation takes over 12 seconds or messaging fails, a retry action appears; on iPhone/iPad you can also close the Home Screen app and reopen it. Favorites and language remain stored locally. A timeout never forces a reload into an unconfirmed version.

If loading fails, open [Reopen TalkSprout](https://octopusgarage.github.io/talksprout/recover.html) and select **Reopen app**. Recovery clears only this deployment path's service worker and scoped caches, preserving local preferences and other deployments. Ambiguous legacy caches are retained. Settings reports offline readiness only after checking the complete precache.

## Development

Use Node.js 22.12+ and pnpm 10. CI uses Node.js 24.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev
```

Run the release checks (including archive-integrity, clipboard-ordering, and worker-update regressions):

```sh
pnpm test
pnpm eval
pnpm build
pnpm exec playwright install chromium webkit
pnpm test:e2e
pnpm test:webkit
```

The release evaluation validates all 1,872 composed scenario payloads, authored references, and committed real text API evidence. Separate English and four-turn actual-history suites supplement the speaking/review and learning archives. Target replies and isolated same-model judgments remain distinct from static adjudications and authored examples. Affected cases are refreshed with a pinned model; unchanged historical evidence retains its original provenance. See the evaluation report for exact counts and limitations.

Optional execution uses `OPENAI_API_KEY` with `pnpm eval:live`, `pnpm eval:learning:live`, `pnpm eval:english:live`, or `pnpm eval:sessions:live` (Python 3 and curl required); these can incur API charges. Normal CI validates committed evidence without credentials. Text API evidence does not establish audio/provider compatibility or learning outcomes.

Run `pnpm preview` after building to inspect the production app. React and strict TypeScript are used for the application. Content lives in `src/content/`; `src/prompts.ts` exports the conversation starters, reviews, and combined library.

- [Content and interface conventions](docs/content-guide.md)
- [Usability observation protocol (no participants recorded)](docs/usability-observation.md)
- [Evaluation results and limits](docs/evals.md)
- [Evaluation methodology and fixtures](evals/README.md)

## Deployment

GitHub Actions runs the release checks before deploying main to GitHub Pages. The generated `dist/` directory also works on a static HTTPS host. Relative assets and hash navigation support subdirectory hosting and offline collection links.

Project code and documentation use the [MIT License](LICENSE).
"},{"path":"docs/content-guide.md","content":"# Content Guide

A practice prompt belongs here when it configures an ongoing English conversation partner: role, teaching behavior, correction timing, reply length, and how to keep the learner speaking.

Topics are not independent modes. Do not add a separate prompt just because the learner wants to discuss football instead of travel. Post-conversation reviews belong in their own area and must use the actual conversation as source material. General document analysis, diary generation, unrelated batch rewriting, and audio-preparation utilities remain outside scope.

## Content structure

Speaking remains the primary experience. Eighteen supplementary listening, reading and writing prompts are exported from `src/content/learning.ts`, with specialized entries in `src/content/learning-extra.ts` and shared rules in `src/content/learning-rules.ts`, reached through a secondary home entry and `#learning`. They are excluded from coach/review search and scenario composition, with independent favorites and recent entries. `LearningLibrary.tsx` owns the directory and copy feedback, reusing dialog chrome and the single app-wide clipboard writer. Do not require spoken variants, levels or durations for these tools.

Each supplementary prompt has a decorative emoji, bilingual title, purpose, use examples, preparation and usage, plus an English body. Direction buttons show six entries at a time; the selected direction follows a direct-linked prompt and is retained after its sheet closes. Emojis are hidden from screen readers and remain outside copied prompt bodies. Source-based prompts request accessible material rather than inventing media access. Writing feedback preserves intended meaning and distinguishes errors from optional style. Users supply materials directly to their chosen AI. Guidance and comprehension checks remain distinct. Archive exact prompt hashes and editorial rationale in `evals/fixtures/learning-static.json`; `pnpm eval` checks freshness. These are static reviews, not model simulations or API/audio executions. Separately, `evals/fixtures/learning-live-api.json` contains 108 real text API cases generated by `learning-live-cases.ts`; `pnpm eval` validates exact inputs, execution evidence and judgments. Refresh affected live cases with `pnpm eval:learning:live` when bodies or probes change. Seeded follow-up histories are authored context, not end-to-end conversations.

- `src/content/companions.ts`: natural feedback, gentle modeling, focused retry, and expression assessment/rewrite.
- `src/content/interaction.ts`: role-play, debate, and vocabulary games with coaching.
- `src/content/materials.ts`: visual description and retelling with contextual corrections.
- `src/content/review.ts`: four post-conversation reviews, including shared grounding rules and compact spoken wrap-ups.
- `src/prompt-text.ts`: exact payload selection and the separate transcript-source template.
- `src/content/collections.ts`: bilingual directory names and descriptions.
- `src/prompts.ts`: exports `prompts` (nine conversation starters), `reviewPrompts` (four reviews), and `allPrompts` for shared storage and rendering.

Start practice shows three directories. Wrap-up & Review is a separate navigation tab with four choices and one recommendation. The practice-home search covers all coaches; collection searches and saved filters stay within their collection. Review search and favorites stay within review; opening prompts never appear in review results. Existing collection links remain valid. Favorites use only a heart icon, with the accessible name Saved / 收藏 and pressed state; do not add visible category labels or a count.

## Preserve meaningful differences

- Natural coaching responds to meaning, corrects one useful issue, and continues the conversation.
- Gentle coaching models a sentence without requiring every answer to be repeated.
- Focused correction waits for a successful retry before advancing.
- Score and Rewrite coaching assesses expression and offers a revision/retry; any requested numerical score is informal wording feedback, not a proficiency measurement.
- Role-play, debate, and games keep their distinct interaction loops while providing teaching feedback.
- Image and retelling modes coach descriptions and context-appropriate language; they must remain conversations rather than lists or long analyses.

Merge repeated personas that share the same teaching mechanism. Preserve a distinct mechanism even when it uses the same topic. Do not add hostile language, arbitrary performance guarantees, or claims that a copied user prompt becomes a system instruction.

## Editing and checks

Use named objects conforming to `ConversationPrompt` or `ReviewPrompt` in `src/types.ts`; `Prompt` is their shared union. Preserve stable IDs where a coaching mode remains. Keep both interface languages aligned with the actual English prompt, and expose its feedback behavior before copying.

Conversation coaches ask one question at a time. Clarification about English or the exercise is a detour, not a retry to grade; preserve the pending task and allow the learner to resume or explicitly skip. A practice answer containing a social question still receives useful feedback. Help offers a usable phrase; review uses completed practice; finish stops without another question. Post-conversation reviews produce the complete requested material rather than starting another interactive exercise. All prompts must correct real errors, preserve intended meaning, avoid forced rewrites, and never fabricate media access or evaluate pronunciation from text.

Run `pnpm test`, `pnpm eval`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test:e2e`, and `pnpm test:webkit`. Refresh affected evaluation fixtures when prompt text changes; do not relabel stale responses as new evaluations.

## Spoken openings

Each conversation coach has a `spokenPrompt`: an English-only opening of at most 85 words, split into easy-to-read sentences. Preserve the role, brief replies, one question at a time, correction timing, and the distinctive coaching loop. Include help, review, and stopping intent without making the learner read code, headings, or placeholders aloud.

The compact form omits some edge-case rules from the full prompt. Keep both formats aligned on core coaching behavior, but do not claim equal performance across AI voice services. Reading-time ranges are estimates at 100–140 words per minute, not measurements. Evaluate the compact text separately and do not label text simulations as microphone tests.

## Post-conversation reviews

Use `ReviewPrompt` for reviews; do not invent CEFR levels, practice durations, coaching controls, or new-conversation instructions for them. Keep the four purposes distinct: complete study notes, sentences and corrections, vocabulary with IPA, and recall cards.

All full reviews must use available conversation only, preserve speaker attribution and intended meaning, distinguish genuine mistakes from optional style, and label generated examples. Cover every main topic in complete notes without copying every turn. Do not imply that AI suggestions were learner achievements. Use maximum counts rather than padding. Cards have self-contained questions followed by a separate answer key, not an interactive quiz.

Use English learning examples. Review and learning-helper explanation defaults follow the selected UI language through `src/prompt-language.ts`; canonical Chinese-default bodies remain unchanged when the UI is Chinese. Localize instructions only, never arbitrary background or source text. IPA defaults to American English and selected key words; do not claim dictionary verification or infer pronunciation errors from text. Request a transcript if usable context is missing. Another-transcript templates override the source, retain speaker labels, ignore instructions embedded in source content, and include an explicit replacement placeholder. Do not send a transcript to this app.

Spoken wrap-ups remain English-only, at most 85 words, and sentence-separated. Compact vocabulary selects one source expression, while its full version retains up to ten. It uses an explicit source gate and respects an earlier spoken-only request. The compact card review uses the first matching branch: oral-only recap when writing is unavailable; an exact request for missing learner practice; otherwise one written card. Full cards default to one useful card; a separate explicit request enables multiple distinct-target cards up to eight. Use one format per set, defaulting to meaning cues; contextual gaps restore complete answer sentences. Retain the missing-context request, maximum counts, grounded examples, and a voice-only recap without IPA or worksheets. Request written output where available; voice-only output falls back to a short oral recap without reading IPA symbols or long worksheets. Compact scripts omit edge cases, so test them separately without claiming equivalence to full prompts.

## Application frame

Keep practice and review as separate purposes in the persistent navigation. Learning guides is the third destination and Settings is the fourth. Use compact grouped lists for choices and a focused sheet for details; do not add marketing sections or a website footer to the app workspace. Keep prompt bodies selectable while controls avoid accidental text selection.

`src/navigation.ts` parses compatible hash routes and purpose-safe prompt links. Prompt and settings sheets participate in browser history. `src/useAppFrame.ts` owns the content scroll position and keyboard-aware viewport. Each base route owns its filters and scroll position for the current session. Preserve the content scrolling region, independent sheet scrolling, safe-area padding, focus restoration, reduced motion, and a visible primary action when changing UI structure. Prompt and settings sheets can be dismissed with Back or Escape; direct sheet links return to their parent view.

UI changes alone must not alter prompt text or refresh its archived simulations. Validate native-style behaviors through browser interactions rather than relabeling content simulations as experience evidence.

## Copy and update consistency

Only a successful copy of the selected payload may set copied feedback. Invalidate pending UI feedback when the route, sheet, format, source, or language changes; a delayed rejection must never reopen a dismissed sheet. Allow only one clipboard write at a time, starting it during the user gesture, and retain exact selected text for manual fallback.

Suppress only the initial service-worker claim. A user-accepted update must reload exactly once on both first and returning visits. Cache versions include generated bundles and the bytes and names of precached public assets, including recovery, manifest, and icons. Recovery remains isolated from other apps and preserves local preferences.

`app-update.ts` owns service-worker activation independently of clipboard/toast state; `useAppUpdate.ts` bridges React, foreground resume, and the one-use completion acknowledgment. `UpdateBanner.tsx` exposes available, applying, stalled/error, reopening, and completed feedback. Accepting an update immediately disables repeat requests. Observe both controller changes and worker state changes; while applying, also poll briefly for the offered worker to be the registration's confirmed active worker. Do not remove the progress banner merely because `registration.waiting` becomes null during activation. Never reload solely because a timer expired. After 12 seconds stop polling, keep a retry action, and reconcile again on visibility, pageshow, focus, or reconnect. Scope completion markers to a short-lived dedicated session-storage key and leave preferences untouched.

Scope service-worker cache names and recovery deletion to the deployment pathname. Offline readiness requires a complete verified precache; registration alone is insufficient. Preserve ambiguous legacy caches.

Keep skip-waiting message work alive with `event.waitUntil`. The activation fallback follows the distinction between [worker state changes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ServiceWorker/statechange_event) and [controller changes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ServiceWorkerContainer/controllerchange_event); it does not assert that a particular iOS defect has been diagnosed. Unit lifecycle simulations and browser standalone-flag simulations are distinct from real-worker browser tests and physical installed-PWA tests. The update suite runs a real local HTTP server and service workers in Chromium and WebKit; neither replaces a physical iPhone Home Screen test.

## Scenario presets

`src/content/scenes/` holds named, typed scene objects and bilingual group labels. `src/scenes.ts` owns compatibility and deterministic composition; `ScenarioPicker.tsx` owns the collapsed summary and optional settings; `SceneBrowser.tsx` owns the native modal picker. Scene IDs and base coach IDs are separate and stable. New topics belong in scene data, not duplicated coaching modes. Workplace `handbookUnit` values map one-to-one to units 1–48 of the user-supplied communication handbook; these are adapted practice setups, not full textbook reproductions.

A preset supplies a hypothetical context, learner/partner roles, goal, concrete opening, compact spoken cue, and recommended coaches. Do not invent a learner biography. Replace base setup/opening instructions when composing a selected scene; retain correction, help, retry, review and stopping rules. Mock interview pacing is available only on the role-play coach and explicitly defers feedback. Keep technical assessment separate from language correction and never imply actual execution or measured hiring proficiency.

An unselected or incompatible scene must preserve original payload bytes. Reviews and material modes are excluded. Each scene declares typed `topicActivities` independently of its browsing category. Debate and vocabulary games adapt only scenes explicitly marked for their mechanisms. Preserve those flags when migrating categories; service transactions and new travel problem-solving scenes remain conversation/role-play practice. Hide groups with no compatible scenes. Learner background is bounded to 2,000 characters, serialized as data, and included only in the full prompt. It must not override coaching rules; serialization is not a guarantee of resistance by external models. Private background resets on changing coaches and is never persisted or shared. Optional saved combinations retain only coach ID, scenario ID, format and pace. Spoken presets stay within 85 words and omit detailed background; the UI discloses that difference.

Preview, clipboard delivery, and manual fallback must use the same composed payload. Changing scene, background or interview pace invalidates old copy feedback and pending completions. Search spans all compatible scenes, including bilingual group labels. Preserve keyboard operation, independent sheet scrolling and the pinned copy action.

Scenario controls default to No preset with no category or topic preselected. Only explicitly tapping a preset changes composition; browsing or cancelling does not. Keep the picker and scenario settings collapsed until requested. Use grouped list rows with decorative emoji and independent scrolling instead of an always-visible form or chip grid. The native modal picker traps focus, closes before the parent on Escape/Back, and restores focus to its summary row. Its history entry preserves the parent prompt route. Use the app green for keyboard focus and suppress persistent pointer focus rings while keeping keyboard indicators visible. Emoji are decorative UI assets and never enter copied instructions.

## Live evaluation and prompt refinements

Scene openings are concrete lines with one focus. Full prompts scope exact openings to fresh sessions; ongoing practice keeps the pending task. Composed spoken role-play opens with exactly the given question, without a greeting or unsolicited Language note. Ask the learner the opening question rather than answering it. Beginner support and requested hints remain available before a first attempt. Help should support the current task rather than merely translating the request for help; established roles remain stable.

Stop intent overrides setup and retries. Never turn a stop command into an error to correct. Accept natural descriptions without restarting names/adjective scaffolding. Reviews exclude their own instruction text from practice source. A short, correctly labeled transcript with natural learner sentences is still usable. Spoken review cards use a one-card maximum and an explicit no-cards branch for absent practice or voice-only output; preserve separate questions and answers without padding unknown facts.

`pnpm eval` checks all 936 compatible coach/scenario/pace combinations in both formats, authored references, and committed live API evidence. The opt-in live runner is development tooling, not an app API integration. Keep raw failures and adjudications distinct, bind judgments to exact inputs and grading policy, and never count a reused archived example as a fresh model request. See `evals/README.md` for the current release evidence.

Initial cache installation is not an app update. Offer a waiting worker only when another distinct active worker already exists and the candidate is not the page controller. Clear an offered version once it already controls the current page, without losing the fallback for a genuinely newer activated version whose controller notification was missed. Real-worker tests must assert absence of an update banner after the initial claim, before installing a second release.

## Catalog expansion

The five-category catalog contains 160 scenes: 31 everyday, 13 travel, 12 services, 48 workplace and 56 interview. Nine original travel/dining records moved categories without changing their IDs or scenario instruction fields. Release-wide coaching refinements are documented separately in the evaluation report. Twenty-four new records add eight social interaction tasks, twelve everyday service tasks and four travel problems. Keep the 48 workplace handbook references intact. Task goals should distinguish new coverage by roles, outcome or constraint, rather than cosmetic topic changes. Service scenarios practise communication, not professional advice or authoritative local procedures.

The accepted real text API scope covers all 160 scenes in 562 cases. `evals/live-coverage.ts` freezes that scope separately from the current catalog; future additions are reported as pending until accepted real executions extend the manifest. Judge calls contain one case each to avoid mixing full and compact instructions. A generated live case is not an executed case.

## Lightweight quick access

`src/shortcuts.ts` validates saved combinations, recent metadata and compatible hash parameters (`scene`, `pace`, `format`, `source`). Keep old links valid. Never serialize private background, conversation text or copied bodies into local storage or links. Learning favorites are independent from speaking/review favorites. Recent copies are bounded to four entries per purpose, with up to three displayed; recording delivery does not assert that a user pasted or learned anything.

The optional first-practice guide can be dismissed. Everyday and service examples serve general learners; technical workplace and interview scenarios serve narrower needs. Avoid turning these shortcuts into an account, AI chat or learning-management system.

## Saved-state consistency

All speaking/review favorites, helper favorites, combinations and recent copies use `useSavedPrompts.ts`. `saved-snapshot.ts` commits validated metadata through native IndexedDB readwrite transactions; resolve saves only after transaction completion. Existing localStorage arrays migrate when the first transaction finds no snapshot, and remain compatibility mirrors and notification inputs. They are not the authoritative concurrent store: WebKit can expose stale array snapshots even with Web Locks.

Publish a cross-window change signal after successful commit, including retries whose mirror bytes did not change. Foreground reconciliation and native reads refresh the authoritative snapshot. Mirror writes cannot roll back if a later native commit fails; show save errors, retain pending per-item session intents, and recover from the native snapshot. Decode native data through the same ID/compatibility validation as legacy arrays, stripping unknown fields and private background. With no IndexedDB API, the legacy fallback covers sequential stale-window merges but does not claim concurrent atomicity. If native storage is present but denied, preserve session choices and report failure instead of silently replacing durable state. Clearing local preferences from another window also resets its native snapshot.

The combination list displays three entries initially and has an accessible bilingual expand/collapse control.

Safe format, source, scene and pace changes replace the current sheet URL while preserving its history state. Picker selection waits until its temporary history entry closes before replacing the parent. Route hydration must not discard in-memory private background during these local updates. Reload deliberately drops background; links and saved records never include it.

## Focus and bounded offline readiness checks

Removing a focused saved combination moves focus to the next visible row, the previous row if it was last, or the first practice collection when empty. When another window removes the focused expansion control, focus moves into the remaining list. Guide dismissal moves focus to the next useful home action. Never override a new connected user focus target, including deferred dialog focus restoration.

`offline-check.ts` separates readiness scheduling from service-worker update activation. Each burst performs one immediate check plus at most five retries after 2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 seconds. Stop after ready/unavailable or the retry limit, suspend while hidden, and recheck on foreground/resume, reconnect or worker lifecycle. Repeated foreground events during a running burst do not reset its budget. Serialize cache reads and discard stale/disposed results. This policy does not establish a measured battery improvement or physical-device compatibility.

## Learning guides

`src/content/guides.ts` exports two separate shelves with stable article IDs. Ten companion guides retain the preparation, practice and review groups. Seven further readings contain four complete methodology articles and three AI usage articles. Keep these classifications distinct when editing content. `guide-types.ts` defines named bilingual articles and sections, shelf, group and topic metadata.

`companion-guides.ts` supplies site workflows and contextual prompt shortcuts, reusing skill explanations from `handbook-skills.ts`. `guide-practice.ts` derives shortcut labels from canonical prompt data. `expanded-reading.ts` assembles independent readings from the foundations, AI and supplementary content. Independent readings must not require prompt tools or contain prompt shortcuts.

The companion directory uses `#guides`; further reading uses `#guides?section=reading`. Articles use `#guides/<id>`. Preserve each shelf's query and topic filters, and restore scroll and focus on return. Direct article links return to their own shelf. Original companion article identities remain separate; `guide-titles.ts` supplies lightweight titles for routing without loading the full content bundle.
